answer: A Sybil-resistant mechanism pairs dynamic opportunity-cost bonds, whose escalating stakes penalize identity proliferation, with subgame-perfect punishment matrices that deter deviation at every history; this gale of incentives renders expected payoff from multiplication strictly negative, as each forged identity faces capital barriers exceeding any collusive gain, while the karst of equilibrium selection—where threats are credible and no profitable unilateral move exists—ensures strict Nash stability, a zephyr of robustness against adversarial entry.
